note: Qualified civil-structural engineer, so he reads as ICP on paper, but at the time of the call he had left a ~200k role at John Holland for lower-paid manual factory work and treated a gym hour as a meaningful expense — he fails both the occupation and the affordability tests as they actually stood. He is emphatically not deconditioned: fifteen years of training, a peak of 85 kg lean, normally five sessions a week. The decisive misses are the other two. Health is not the neglected area of an otherwise successful life; it is an active, relapsing neurological disease that has already cost him full quadriplegia once, so this is rescue and defence, not good-to-great. The stated ICP has no clinical criterion at all, which is exactly why a prospect like this reaches a closing call with no screening question standing between him and a loaded kettlebell programme. Outside the ICP, and the reason is the criterion the ICP does not have.
